objective: Test whether structural occurrence context gives a shared common triangle carrier, and whether one GF(2) scalar functional can serve pooled matched dependencies across all three carriers.
contextDefinition: For every canonical vertex triangle in the union observed structural catalog, record the 3-bit set of carriers in which it occurs. This support profile is structural and contains no scalar values.

candidates.definition: Augment each of the four PMEC triangle keys with the fixed structural occurrence profile, then join the four equality partitions. Use the resulting shared triangle components for every carrier.
Direct sum of the RS081 local triangle maps, tagging each feature with its declared carrier label. This is a reconstruction control, not the desired common law.

procedure: Use only committed RS079/RS080/RS081 structural snapshots for preparation. Freeze all shared catalogs, occurrence profiles, rows and bases before replay.
Concatenate the three declared carrier dependency lists in their fixed order. Check each existing scalar code gauge is identical before pooled qualification.
Measure per-carrier ranks and exactness, pooled structural rank, pooled scalar consistency, and explicit cross-carrier kernel certificates.
Persist and commit structure before replaying aligned pinned RS077 scalar codes. Do not fit or publish a coefficient decoder.

A pooled contradiction is a scoped obstruction to a single linear functional on that shared carrier. It does not exclude nonlinear composition, geometry-conditioned laws, or a different native structural carrier.
rationale: Equalities generated within a fixed occurrence profile cannot use triangles absent from any carrier in that profile. This contextual construction refines every local common partition on its carrier, without scalar-selected splits. Its empirical domain is still a limitation to explain, not a final formula.
